description: Advanced and mixed C Programming questions for competitive and examination practice

questions.questionText: Which preprocessor directive is used to include a header file?
questions.explanation: The #include directive is used to include the contents of a header file.

questions.questionText: Which preprocessor directive is used to define a macro?
questions.explanation: The #define directive is used to define macros.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? #define PI 3.14 int main() { printf("%.2f", PI); }
questions.explanation: The preprocessor replaces PI with 3.14 before compilation.

questions.questionText: Which directive is used for conditional compilation when a macro is defined?
questions.explanation: #ifdef checks whether a specified macro has been defined.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to open a file in C?
questions.explanation: The fopen() function opens a file and returns a FILE pointer.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to close an opened file?
questions.explanation: fclose() closes a file that was opened using a standard C file function.

questions.questionText: Which file mode opens a file for reading?
questions.explanation: The mode "r" opens an existing file for reading.

questions.questionText: Which file mode opens a file for writing and creates it if it does not exist?
questions.explanation: The "w" mode opens a file for writing and creates it if necessary; an existing file is truncated.

questions.questionText: Which file mode opens a file for appending data at the end?
questions.explanation: The "a" mode opens a file for appending. New data is written at the end of the file.

questions.questionText: Which function is commonly used to write formatted output to a file?
questions.explanation: fprintf() writes formatted output to a specified stream, including a file.

questions.questionText: Which function is commonly used to read formatted input from a file?
questions.explanation: fscanf() reads formatted input from a specified stream.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to write a character to a file stream?
questions.explanation: fputc() writes a single character to a specified output stream.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to read a character from a file stream?
questions.explanation: fgetc() reads the next character from a specified input stream.

questions.questionText: What does EOF generally represent in C file input operations?
questions.explanation: EOF stands for End Of File and is used to indicate that no more input can be read from a stream.

questions.questionText: Which parameter of main() can be used to receive command-line arguments?
questions.explanation: The conventional form int main(int argc, char *argv[]) provides command-line argument information.

questions.questionText: What does argc represent in a conventional command-line main function?
questions.explanation: argc contains the number of command-line arguments, including the program name.

questions.questionText: What does argv represent in a conventional command-line main function?
questions.optionC: An integer containing the argument count
questions.optionD: An array of strings containing command-line arguments
questions.explanation: argv is an array of pointers to strings containing the command-line arguments.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 5; printf("%d", x++ + ++x);
questions.explanation: The variable x is modified more than once without the required sequencing between the evaluations, resulting in undefined behavior.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 10; if(x = 0) printf("Yes"); else printf("No");
questions.explanation: x = 0 is an assignment expression whose value is 0, so the if condition is false and No is printed.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int x = 5; printf("%d", x > 3 && x < 10);
questions.explanation: Both conditions are true, so the logical AND expression evaluates to 1.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a = 5, b = 2; printf("%d", a / b);
questions.explanation: Both operands are integers, so integer division is performed and 5 / 2 gives 2.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a = 5; printf("%d", a << 1);
questions.explanation: For this positive integer, shifting 5 left by one bit gives 10.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int a = 5; printf("%d", a & 3);
questions.explanation: 5 is 101 in binary and 3 is 011. 101 & 011 gives 001, which is 1.

questions.questionText: Which storage class specifies that a variable is defined elsewhere, usually in another source file?
questions.explanation: The extern keyword declares that an object or function is defined elsewhere.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a C function is correct?
questions.optionA: A function can call itself directly or indirectly
questions.optionB: Every function must have at least one parameter
questions.optionC: A function can never call another function
questions.explanation: A function may call another function and may also call itself, which is recursion.
